analysis:
Examined the two base-text units of ClusterService.swift (lines 911-1536): the update check, approval check, status publication, supervise loop, partEnvironment, removeEndedApproval, leaderAPIPort and stopChild. The visible PR changes are in other line ranges, which I only see through a truncated patch excerpt: `responder` made non-private, new `responderCheck`/`controlCheck` replacing the cable check, a new `listening: Listening` init parameter, and listener changes around head lines 337-401. I cannot see those head-side lines, so I cannot assess the new listener or pairing-check behavior.

The supplied base code does not show a new regression. The cluster approval and update paths take ClusterControlCommandLock, and the approval path re-decides under the lock. The part environment redirects the heartbeat file. Log files are created 0600, and the service-status and supervision files are written atomically in the owner's own directory.

The threat model has no cluster-specific boundary. The nearest ones are TB-003 (operator versus process), TB-002 (coordinator link) and T-041 (prefix cache). The cacheSync/leaderPin handling at line 935 touches prefix-cache settings propagated between Macs, but the supplied lines show no change to it.

Open question for the next pass: whether the new Listening injection, the now-internal `responder` and the `listenerChange` pairing checks (head side, lines 144-175 and 337-420) weaken peer authentication or expose a listener on an unintended interface. Those head-side lines were not supplied, so the conclusion is limited to the base lines shown.
